headlines.title: Small plane carrying 2 people crashes near Petaluma Municipal Airport
headlines.description: A small plane carrying two people crashed in a field near the Petaluma Municipal Airport late Wednesday morning, according to the FAA. The conditions of the two people were not immediately known. The Van’s RV-7A went down at about 10:45 a.m. shortly after taking off from the airport, according to the FAA. An investigation is underway. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: 2 dead after house fire in Monte Sereno
headlines.description: Two older adults died after being rescued from a house fire in Monte Sereno early Wednesday morning, according to the Santa Clara County Fire Department. Firefighters responded around 2 a.m. to a reported structure fire at a home in the 17000 block of Rose Court. When crews arrived, they found a two-story home with flames coming through the roof. A second alarm was called, bringing the response to 10 fire apparatus and approximately 40 fire personnel. Firefighters experienced problems getting into the home, and there were no working smoke alarms, officials said. Once inside, crews located and rescued two older adults. Both patients were taken by ambulance to Valley Medical Center, where they later died from their injuries, fire officials said. The identities of the two people who died have not yet been released. The cause of the fire remains under investigation by the Santa Clara County Fire Department with assistance from other local agencies. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

headlines.title: Grandmother in Monterey County ‘Baby Angelita' incest case arrested
headlines.description: A grandmother of a newborn baby found dead in a suspected incest case in Monterey County in August was arrested on suspicion of multiple crimes, the sheriff’s office said Tuesday. Ofelia Garcia Ortega, 36, was served with an arrest warrant Tuesday at a courthouse in Salinas on suspicion of displaying or possessing a forged identification card, permitting a child to suffer or be endangered, and contributing to the delinquency of a minor. The case involves Garcia Ortega’s 14-year-old daughter and the teen’s father, Sergio Galvez Perez, who is suspected of impregnating the girl. According to the Monterey County District Attorney’s Office on Tuesday, the investigation also examined Garcia Ortega’s conduct involving her daughter. Investigators determined Garcia Ortega allegedly put her daughter to work in agricultural fields at age 13 using falsified documentation, allowed her to drive without a license, and allowed her to remain completely out of school. The sheriff’s office believes that Galvez Perez committed incest against his teen daughter and that she abandoned an infant who was fathered by him shortly after giving birth a little over two months ago. Authorities have named the deceased infant “Baby Angelita.” On Sunday, the sheriff’s office received confirmation that the daughter had been rescued by Mexican law enforcement and that her father was arrested. An Amber Alert had gone out on Sept. 6 for the pair. The case garnered a lot of attention after Sheriff Tina Nieto initially announced that there was probable cause to arrest the teen for murder. The sheriff’s office also initially said the case did not meet the right criteria for an Amber Alert to be issued. Pushback from Supervisor Wendy Root Askew and the community led the district attorney’s office to release a statement that it hadn’t charged the girl with anything. Prosecutors have however filed charges against Galvez Perez “for the heinous crime of sexually assaulting his own child.” Crime and Courts Oct 4 Amber Alert Sep 6 Amber Alert issued for teen girl, father wanted in connection with infant death
headlines.source: Katy St. Clair | Bay City News

headlines.title: Community shows support following hate crime at San Anselmo elementary school
headlines.description: North Bay community members gathered Tuesday night to show their support for an elementary school that was the target of a hate crime. On Saturday night, someone wrote “I hate Jews” and drew a swastika on the asphalt at Brookside Elementary School in San Anselmo, Central Marin police said. The graffiti was quickly removed, but many families were left shaken. On Tuesday, the San Anselmo town council held a community gathering at the school. They encouraged neighbors to write messages of love and belonging. Anita Frank, a Holocaust survivor, emphasized the importance of the community coming together and speaking out against hate. “We recognize when there is hatred against any group, there is hatred towards us all, that we’re all connected, we’re all related,” she said. “There is only one race, the human race. In San Anselmo, this beautiful occasion happened where we all united as a community, and that was so powerful for me, so important to me.” No arrests have been made in the case. A $10,000 reward is being offered.

headlines.title: Morgan Hill man accused of killing wife due in court
headlines.description: A South Bay man accused of killing his wife, possibly in front of three children, is expected to appear in a Santa Clara County courtroom Wednesday afternoon. The woman was identified as 34-year-old Jasmyne Garcia, a Salinas native described as a loving mother, daughter and sister, according to a GoFundMe launched to help the victim’s family. Her husband, 37-year-old Roy Lopez, is expected to face a judge on a murder charge. Video posted on social media showed Lopez arriving at Good Samaritan Hospital in San Jose, about 20 miles from the home where he told investigators he killed his wife. Lopez was arrested by San Jose police and turned over to Morgan Hill police for questioning, during which he allegedly confessed to killing his wife. “His admission to killing his wife will be the centerpiece of this case,” legal analyst Steven Clark said. “It’s also important, the manner of the killing. Certainly the defense team can argue, if he intended to kill his wife, why did he drive her to the hospital?” Court documents reviewed by NBC Bay Area show Lopez was arrested in 2014 for allegedly raping a woman in Gilroy, but the charges were eventually dropped. Court documents also show Lopez was arrested for battery against a woman in 2010. In that case, he was ultimately sentenced to volunteer work. The three children found in the home after the homicide are safe and in protective custody. Police say the children, ages 14, 6 and 3, may have witnessed the attack on their mother. Lopez is due in court at 1:30 p.m. Wednesday. If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline by calling 1-800-799-SAFE (7233), visiting www.thehotline.org or texting LOVEIS to 22522. headlines.title: San Francisco supervisors pass temporary moratorium on data centers
headlines.description: San Francisco on Tuesday became the first county in the Bay Area to enact a temporary moratorium on the construction of new data centers. The Board of Supervisors voted unanimously at its regular meeting to approve a 45-day urgency ordinance that took effect immediately. The moratorium calls for a halt to the approval of permit applications to expand an existing data center or build a new one, which house the computing hardware and infrastructure needed to power newly developed artificial intelligence tools. Newer data centers are also referred to as AI data centers and are similar to data centers of the past that house servers, storage systems, and networking equipment, according to IBM. But the computing demands of AI and generative AI that produce text and images require more equipment that also uses more power and requires a source of water to cool overheating servers and other components. The excessive energy and water use, combined with noise complaints and water supply contamination, prompted the moratorium to be proposed by District 10 Supervisor Shamann Walton. “During this period, we will be looking at issues including energy, water, air quality, land use, and community impacts, while working towards stronger protections and meaningful community input, as well as ‘data center’ definition that is clear to everyone,” he said at the board meeting. Over a dozen commenters spoke in support of the moratorium when the ordinance was introduced at the Land Use and Transportation Committee meeting on Monday. Walton said at Tuesday’s meeting that the moratorium would give the city the opportunity to better understand the environmental and local impacts data centers create. “We are seeing data centers pop up near residential communities all across the United States, and we have seen the impacts from polluting the water supply, to the noise these facilities bring to neighborhoods closest to them,” Walton said at the committee meeting. He said there had been no community input or transparency when a data center was recently approved on Paul Avenue, in his district, which includes Bayview-Hunters Point. He said the approval was given in 2016 under outdated planning conditions that needed to be updated. Walton said the number of data centers in the city was unknown, partially because the city lacked a comprehensive definition of what they were, something he said the moratorium would address by giving the board time to draft long-term regulations. The city’s Planning Department currently categorizes them as an “internet service exchange,” which was previously understood to be any component that facilitated the networking of computer systems. But he said existing data centers in the city were concentrated in Bayview-Hunters Point and the South of Market neighborhood, which Walton said have historically taken on a disproportionate amount of the city’s industrial pollution. The ordinance authored by Walton uses the definition used by U.S. Senator Alex Padilla in legislation he wrote seeking greater federal regulation of data centers, which defines them as “a facility, or part of a facility, that houses computing infrastructure, including graphics and central processing units, servers, storage devices, networking equipment, and associated power and cooling systems, for the primary purpose of processing, storing, or distributing electronic data.” Supervisor Matt Dorsey proposed clarifying amendments that stipulated that the moratorium does not apply to businesses that have server rooms dedicated to onsite operations, rather than those that serve offsite customers’ data needs.

headlines.title: Sparkling from head to toe, amputee Cynthia Cheak becomes a key face of Valkyries' ‘Ballhalla' crowd
headlines.description: Sparkling and sequined in the Valkyries’ violet colors from head to toe, down to her cane and prosthetic left leg, Cynthia Cheak reaches into a cross-body bag and pulls out a handful of Golden State playoff-themed bracelets she bought to share all around the arena. Then the 68-year-old Cheak begins her nightly ritual of walking through Chase Center giving them away. Always with a smile and signature message: “Hi, guys, want your swag? You’ve got to have swag. You’ve got to wear it. If you don’t wear it, we don’t win.” The second-year WNBA franchise has given Cheak new life. A former personal trainer in Berkeley, she was struggling both emotionally and physically after losing her left leg two years ago. An amputation became necessary to keep her alive. Cheak had undergone knee replacement surgery in 2020 and dealt with an infection a week later, then nine surgeries and numerous antibiotics didn’t heal her. A fall early last year led to yet another operation — No. 11 in total — on the amputated leg. She was lost. “That’s when the depression really got bad,” she said. Finding new purpose Four months later, the Valkyries began playing and would make history becoming the first expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its inaugural season. Cheak was hooked. Now, Golden State is in the WNBA semifinals with a 1-0 lead over the defending champion Las Vegas Aces going into Wednesday’s Game 2. Cheak is cheering away, a beloved regular face among the team’s diverse and vibrant “Ballhalla” home crowd — a play on Valhalla from Norse mythology. Once she’s inside Chase Center, Cheak can let go of her own challenges for a few hours and her mood instantly improves, knowing she is uplifting others each time she arrives to make new friends and greet old ones. She hugs children and poses for photos. “It’s euphoric when I come here,” she said. “Just the response of helping people, it’s amazing.” She’s always surprised to be recognized at Starbucks, Costco, the doctor’s office. “It’s a hoot,” Cheak said. Valkyries guard Kaitlyn Chen, who won an NCAA championship with Connecticut last year before being drafted by Golden State, signed Cheak’s glittery prosthetic leg. There will be another one on order once Cheak can get all the players to provide their autographs to be laminated on the socket. “I wasn’t sure I was going to walk again or be able to come to a game, and so the Valkyries … were really encouraging for me,” she said. “I didn’t want to come in with crutches or anything, so they just helped me get over the stuff, the mass depression I had about having no leg.” “It was so encouraging, I’ve been here ever since,” she said. “Now I’m an advocate for disabled, and passing out swag.” Cheak has handed out some 20,000 bracelets since she started in June, and more than 8,000 of the playoff version over the past four games. She ordered more after the Game 1 victory. The Valkyries are inspired by their fan’s courage And, while Cheak has been inspired by the Valkyries, they have felt the same way seeing her courage to come back. Chen loves her, after meeting Cheak just briefly. “She’s such joy, she’s just always smiling and so happy and she put a smile on my face,” Chen said. “It was pretty cool to be able to meet her. I feel like stories like hers are so incredible. It almost amazes me how much of an impact that we could have on other people’s lives, and that really warms my heart and makes me happy.” “The Bay Area has sort of taken us in and I feel like they’ve changed our lives as much as we’ve changed theirs.” Once the Valkyries clinched a playoff berth on Aug. 17 by beating the Dallas Wings, Cheak had already ordered the playoff-themed bracelets, so they were ready to hand out the very next game two days later. When coach Natalie Nakase heard about Cheak’s story, she immediately dedicated that clinching game to her team’s loyal fan. “We’re playing for Cynthia,” Nakase said. “The fact that she was able to transition into a better state, that’s not easy for all of us who are human beings and we have really low days or states.” In “Ballhalla,” it’s about everyone feeling equal. Cheak sees the joy from her giving, sure, but knows her presence matters in bringing awareness to the amputee community. “The Valkyries were so inspirational for me,” said Cheak, who still trains dementia patients while also doing her own strength work overseen by a trainer three days a week. She continues to make people smile every step of the way. Like fellow Valkyries fan Lauren Wu, who has gone through her own health ordeal. “Not only is she the sparkle queen over here with her sparkle theme, sparkle everything, she is the absolute bracelet fairy,” said Wu, whose two daughters wear their wristbands from Cheak regularly. “It means something, it really does. It’s the spirit of the whole community here, how giving everyone is.” For Cheak, there has been one motivation: “This year, I want to spread the love.” ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

headlines.title: Bay Area renters face rising prices, fewer options in tight rental market
headlines.description: Finding an apartment to rent is getting harder in parts of the Bay Area, with renters facing rising prices and fewer options, according to a new report. The online rental marketplace Zumper published its 2026 Renter Leverage Index, which measures where renters have the most negotiating power. Nationwide, renters gained leverage in a majority of markets, but the Bay Area moved in the opposite direction. San Francisco ranked 43rd out of 44 cities nationwide, with its grade dropping from a “C” to an “F.” San Jose ranked 40th, dropping from a “C” to a “D.” Zumper believes the local economic boom tied to the growing artificial intelligence industry could be contributing to the scarcity of rentals in the South Bay. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Sonoma County officials declare emergency ahead of possible wet winter
headlines.description: Sonoma County officials are stepping up preparations for a potentially wet winter, declaring an emergency Tuesday as forecasters warn that a strong El Niño could bring unusually heavy rain. The Board of Supervisors proclaimed the emergency as the county prepares for a season that could bring flooding, mudslides and other storm-related problems. The action comes two weeks after Gov. Gavin Newsom issued a statewide emergency proclamation, saying the anticipated impacts could require resources from multiple jurisdictions and mutual aid regions. Forecasters put the chance of El Niño reaching historic levels this winter at 75%, according to the county. “The best time to prepare for a flood is before a storm,” Supervisor Rebecca Hermosillo, chair of the Board of Supervisors, said in a statement released by the county. County crews are already clearing culverts and flood-control channels and checking roads and other areas that have flooded or experienced slides in the past. Crews are also staging sandbags, barricades and other equipment. Emergency managers are preparing for increased staffing and emergency operations, while rainfall, stream and reservoir monitoring systems are being readied for the winter. The emergency proclamation directs county departments, Sonoma Water and sanitation districts to create a prioritized list of threatened or vulnerable infrastructure. It also calls for coordination with cities, special districts, tribal partners and state emergency managers.

headlines.title: Hockey community honors San Carlos crash victim on what would have been his 59th birthday
headlines.description: A little more than a month after a San Carlos man was killed by a wrong-way driver in a fiery crash, his community came together to celebrate what would have been his 59th birthday. Steve Hinkson was killed in late August in a crash on Montague Expressway at the Lafayette Street overpass in Santa Clara by a wrong-way driver who also died. The biotech manager had been out grabbing sandwiches for his team. The Santa Clara Police Department said the crash remains an active investigation as authorities await the full report from the medical examiner’s office. But instead of focusing solely on the tragedy, loved ones gathered Tuesday night at the Nazareth Ice Oasis in Foster City for a hockey party in his honor. Flannels on, friends and family played a game where the final score didn’t matter. They ate, asked “What the puck, Steve?” and celebrated the man who always put his wife and two daughters first. “Everyone said, ‘You know what? That felt like Steve, he was here with us, that was Steve,'” said Anna Ison, Hinkson’s widow. Ison noted that his last text in the family thread wished his girls a good first day at UC Berkeley and told them he loved them. “Sometimes it feels like it’s hard to breathe,” Ison said. “Things just aligned in a certain way that put him in a place and time that took him away from us.” At work, Hinkson was remembered as intuitive and smart. Lisa Hazen, one of his former colleagues, said, “I always had him interview people that I was trying to hire because he would ask very unique questions, and I figured if they could pass his test, then they were good to go.” Later in life, Hinkson picked up hockey after meeting Anna. Though his size could be intimidating, friends on the ice knew him differently. “A gentle giant,” said family friend Laura Johnston. “It’s such a tragic loss, and we all miss Steve immensely, and we’re all here to support Anna, but I think that today is a wonderful example of how the hockey community really comes together.” Whether stepping up to a karaoke microphone with his hockey friends or focusing on his family, Hinkson seemingly spent his life thinking of others. “His life was full of meaning, and full of love, and full of purpose. He was himself through it all until the very end,” Ison said. “Today, I feel like, ‘You know what, bud? It’s my turn. I am doing something to make you happy, and it’s making me happy.'” Steve’s hockey stick remains outside the rink for now—a quiet, enduring reminder for those who loved him that he is still skating alongside them.

headlines.title: San Jose police detain barricaded suspect, rescue two juveniles unharmed on Meadow Glen Way
headlines.description: An armed or barricade incident involving an adult male suspect and two juveniles in San Jose’s 1500 block of Meadow Glen Way concluded safely Tuesday morning after the suspect was taken into custody by police. The San Jose Police Department reported the active incident at 9:12 a.m., stating that officers responded to the residence for a welfare check. Upon arrival, authorities found that an adult male suspect had barricaded himself inside a home with two juveniles. Officers established a perimeter and began attempting to negotiate a peaceful surrender. The standoff ended successfully when the suspect was taken into custody and both juveniles were rescued unharmed. Further details regarding the suspect’s identity and potential charges have not yet been released as the investigation continues.

headlines.title: Man arrested on suspicion of arson after Alameda apartment fire
headlines.description: A 52-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson following a fast-moving apartment fire in Alameda early Wednesday morning, police said. Police identified the suspect as Bernard Collins. Several residents at the Surf Apartments told NBC Bay Area that Collins lived in the first-floor unit where the fire started and had threatened to burn the complex down before the fire. Cellphone video from a resident showed flames shooting out of the first-floor unit. The video also showed Collins in the parking lot. The fire spread from the first-floor unit to units on the second and third floors, where three adults were trapped. Firefighters rescued the three residents, and one was taken to a hospital. A fourth resident jumped from the third floor to escape. A neighbor said that person suffered a broken ankle. Jose Mercado, who lived next door to Collins, escaped his unit with his two young daughters. “This tenant has been a problem,” Mercado said. Alameda fire officials said six units were damaged or destroyed and 12 residents were displaced. The Red Cross was at the scene offering displaced residents financial assistance for a hotel, food and clothing in the short term. Residents will also be assigned caseworkers for longer-term assistance. Alameda fire officials said the fire remains under investigation.
headlines.source: NBC Bay Area staff and Bob Redell
